# Nehemiah Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 471v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now there arose a great outcry from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.

**2** Some said, "With our sons and our daughters, we are many. Let us get grain, that we may eat and survive."

**3** Others said, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses to get grain because of the famine."

**4** Still others said, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

**5** Now our flesh is the same as our brothers' flesh, our children the same as their children. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters have already been enslaved — and we are powerless, for our fields and vineyards belong to others."

**6** I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.

**7** I took counsel with myself, then brought charges against the nobles and the officials. I said to them, "You are exacting interest, each from his own brother!" And I called a great assembly against them.

**8** I said to them, "As far as we were able, we have bought back our Jewish brothers who had been sold to the nations. But you are even selling your own brothers, only for them to be sold back to us!" They fell silent and could find nothing to say.

**9** I said, "What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to prevent the reproach of the nations, our enemies?

**10** Moreover, I and my brothers and my servants have been lending them money and grain. Let us stop this exacting of interest.

**11** Return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive orchards, and their houses, and the interest on the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been exacting from them."

**12** They said, "We will return these and will require nothing from them. We will do as you say." So I called the priests and made them take an oath to do as they had promised.

**13** I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not keep this promise. So may he be shaken out and emptied." And all the assembly said "Amen" and praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised.

**14** Moreover, from the day I was appointed governor in the land of Judah — from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years — neither I nor my brothers ate the food allowance of the governor.

**15** The former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people, taking from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants lorded it over the people. But I did not do so, out of the fear of God.

**16** I also devoted myself to the work on this wall, and we acquired no land. All my servants were gathered at the work.

**17** Moreover, a hundred and fifty Jews and officials ate at my table, besides those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

**18** What was prepared each day was one ox, six choice sheep, and birds; and every ten days, all kinds of wine in abundance. Yet for all this, I did not demand the food allowance of the governor, for the burden of labor was heavy on this people.

**19** Remember me for good, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Nehemiah 5 shifts from external threats to internal injustice, revealing that the community's greatest danger may come from within. The chapter exposes a crisis of covenant economics: wealthy Jews are charging interest to fellow Jews and seizing their land and children as collateral — practices explicitly forbidden by Torah. Nehemiah's response is swift and comprehensive: he confronts the powerful, secures public oaths, and then offers his own twelve-year record of sacrificial leadership as a model. The "remember me" prayer in the final verse is not self-congratulation but a covenant appeal, asking God to witness faithfulness as He promised to do.

---

## Disagreement Log

### V.5 — "enslaved" vs. "subjected" vs. "sold into slavery"
- **EMET:** "subjecting" (*koveshim*) / **LOGOS:** "forcing into slavery" / **PNEUMA:** "sell into slavery"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "forcing into slavery" — The Hebrew *kavash* means to subdue or subjugate; "slavery" makes the covenant violation explicit for English readers. EMET's "subjecting" is too mild.

### V.11 — "the hundredth" vs. "the percentage" vs. "the interest"
- **EMET:** "the-hundredth" (*me'at*) / **LOGOS:** "the percentage" / **PNEUMA:** "the interest"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the interest" — While *me'at* likely refers to a specific rate (perhaps 1% monthly), "interest" communicates the economic reality clearly. The exact rate is debated; precision here would be speculative.

### V.15 — "because of the fear of God" vs. "out of the fear of God" vs. "out of reverence for God"
- **EMET:** "because-of the-fear of-God" / **LOGOS:** "because of the fear of God" / **PNEUMA:** "out of reverence for God"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "out of the fear of God" — Slightly more natural English than EMET/LOGOS while preserving the Hebrew *yir'at Elohim*. PNEUMA's "reverence" softens the force of *yir'ah* in a context where fear of divine judgment is the explicit motivation.

---

*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
